investigations.name: quantum-multi-omic-classifier
investigations.title: Quantum Multi-Omic Classifier — Genotype-to-Phenotype Mapping via Data Re-Uploading
investigations.description: This investigation evaluates the GenotypeToPhenotypeProcess — an M-qubit data-reuploading quantum classifier where each qubit encodes one omic modality (genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics). A CNOT chain entangles all modality qubits, enabling the circuit to learn cross-modality interactions natively. Performance is benchmarked against Random Forest and Logistic Regression on synthetic and (eventually) real v2ecoli zarr data.
investigations.question: Can a multi-qubit, cross-modality entangled quantum classifier outperform classical ML baselines in predicting binary phenotypes from synthetic multi-omic data?
investigations.hypothesis: The entanglement-based architecture will capture cross-modality interactions more effectively than classical methods, yielding higher AUC-ROC on held-out test sets, especially when nonlinear interactions between modalities drive phenotype.
